clue.text: Component of arm certain to be rejected after stink

indicators.note: the reversed word comes after the stink in the answer

parts.note: to hum is British slang for to smell bad

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the word for certain is read backwards

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: A medical note: some part of the arm has been dismissed because of a foul smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be rejected' signals a reversal of the word for certain; hum for a bad smell is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the long bone of the upper arm, running from shoulder to elbow, so a component of the limb.

clue.text: Activity linked to drawing room, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word for room is said aloud and sounds like the answer

parts.note: a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: A pastime associated with the drawing room, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing room' looks like one phrase; split it, 'drawing' ends the definition and 'room' is HALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul is to pull or drag, and drawing in the sense of pulling is the same action.

clue.text: Purcell's particular note?

parts.note: the composer's surname has seven letters and the one in the centre is a C, which is also a note name

explanation.surface: A question about a note the composer Henry Purcell favoured.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical note at the centre of the keyboard is also, as letters, the centre of the name PurCell.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the C nearest the centre of the piano keyboard, and here also the central letter of the composer's name.

clue.text: Another chance to see sport through curtailed opening

a curtailed word has its tail, the last letter, cut off

parts.note: a rent is a tear or opening
RU is short for rugby union

explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like the start of a show; it is a rent, a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat broadcast of a programme gives viewers another chance to watch it.

clue.text: Lower back pain? Spies a nervous response in it

parts.note: it, like SA, is old slang for sex appeal
the CIA is the US spy agency
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Agents twitch nervously over some backache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal is a crossword convention, from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sciatica is pain along the sciatic nerve, felt in the lower back, hip and leg.

clue.text: Cross cat's sound recalled sound of bird

parts.note: chi is the Greek letter shaped like a cross, X

indicators.note: called back, so the cat's noise is read from the end

parts.note: a contented cat purrs

explanation.surface: An angry cat's noise is remembered as being like a bird's call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry'; it is the Greek letter CHI. 'recalled' turns PURR into RRUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirrup is the short high twittering call of a small bird such as a sparrow.

clue.text: Force Frenchmen out of business

indicators.note: the Frenchmen are taken out of the word for business

parts.note: commerce is trade or business
MM abbreviates messieurs, French for gentlemen

explanation.surface: Drive French gentlemen out of their trade.
explanation.walkthrough: MM is the French plural abbreviation for Messieurs, the plural of Monsieur.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce is to compel someone by threats or pressure.

clue.text: I note rising worry over one contact

indicators.note: in a down entry, the earlier pieces sit over, above, the last one

parts.note: N for note is a common abbreviation

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word for worry is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to fret is to worry
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Someone noting growing anxiety about a single contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns FRET into TERF, and 'over' puts the earlier pieces above ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An interface is a point where two systems meet and touch, a place of contact.

clue.text: Runs to the front of old plain dome

indicators.note: the runs letter moves from inside to the front of the old plain

parts.note: a tundra is a vast treeless Arctic plain
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to the front of an old flat dome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the front of' moves the R of OTUNDRA to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building or hall topped by a dome, so the dome stands for it.

clue.text: Power line here's flapping, ready for grasping

indicators.note: flapping means agitated, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A power cable here is swinging loose and almost in reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapping' shuffles LINE HERES to REHENSILE, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A monkey's tail that can grip branches is described this way: adapted for seizing and holding.

clue.text: Oppressed by false story about new mark

parts.note: to be under someone is to be oppressed by them

indicators.note: the false story goes round the abbreviation for new

parts.note: a lie is a false story

explanation.walkthrough: 'mark' is a verb here, to mark by stressing, not a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline a word is to mark it with a stroke beneath, for emphasis.

clue.text: Right time to don hat?

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the hat is worn round the time letter

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Is this the proper moment to put on one's hat?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to don' makes the hat, TILE, go round T. Tile for a hat is old British slang, chiefly for a top hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a right or legal claim, as in title to a property.

clue.text: Finger given by this less restrained element?

parts.note: the second word of the answer jumbled, with the first word as a crazy anagram signal, would give the word Finger

explanation.surface: A rude gesture made by members of a wild extremist faction.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, the answer says 'rearrange FRINGE wildly', which gives FINGER: the clue names the result, not the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the extreme, wild members of a political or social group, the least restrained part.

clue.text: Morning burden? Support embracing wife in evening, mostly

indicators.note: the support with the wife inside goes into the shortened evening
mostly means the word for evening loses its last letter

parts.note: dusk is evening twilight

indicators.note: the support word goes round the wife letter

parts.note: an anchor is a mainstay or support

explanation.walkthrough: 'burden' means a song's refrain, not a load. 'embracing' makes AWNCHOR; 'mostly' cuts DUSK to DUS, which goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The birdsong at daybreak is a morning song, and a burden is an old word for a song's refrain.

clue.text: Faithfulness — a leading feature of crucial church role

indicators.note: the leading feature of a word is its first letter, here taken from crucial

parts.note: a curacy is the post of a curate in the church

explanation.surface: Loyalty seen as the chief quality of a vital post in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading feature of' picks the first letter of 'crucial'; a curacy is a curate's office, an assistant priest's post.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithfulness to an original, as in a faithful copy, is exactness or correctness.

clue.text: Research formerly capturing an echo effect

parts.note: RES is a standard abbreviation for research

indicators.note: the word for formerly takes the word an inside it

parts.note: once means formerly

explanation.surface: Past research has picked up an echoing effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' is taken just as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonance is a deep reverberating quality in sound, like an echo that lingers.

clue.text: French port regrettably claiming half of Channel Islands?

parts.note: C, the first half of CI, the abbreviation for Channel Islands

indicators.note: only one half of the islands' abbreviation is taken inside the exclamation; the other stands in front

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning regrettably
I, the second half of CI, the abbreviation for Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A French harbour sadly laying claim to some of Britain's Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: CI is the usual abbreviation for the Channel Islands. 'claiming half of' puts only its I inside ALAS; the C stays outside in front, which the blog's commenters found loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Calais is the ferry port on France's north coast, facing Dover across the Strait.

clue.text: Evasive action that is needed in a month

parts.note: Sep is short for September
id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.walkthrough: Latin 'id est', abbreviated i.e., is written out in full for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep is to dodge by stepping aside, an evasive move.

clue.text: Daughter is coming in nearly frozen — having tried this?

nearly means not quite the whole word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: numb with cold, frozen

explanation.definitionFit: Being nearly frozen is what you would expect after practising naked outdoor living, so the definition reads off the rest of the clue.

clue.text: Goddess satisfied to block Diana's target?

met, as in met a demand, means satisfied

explanation.walkthrough: Diana is the Roman goddess of hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeter is the Greek goddess of the harvest and corn, mother of Persephone.

clue.text: Dismiss dance as a transient flashy thing

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone sacks a dance as a passing showy fad.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireball is a bright meteor or burst of flame, flaring briefly and then gone.

clue.text: An unfortunate situation besets most of the colony

parts.note: an ill is a misfortune

indicators.note: most of the word means it loses its last letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts THE to TH, which AN and ILL surround.

clue.text: Mother in love, in pursuit of a sensual man

the mother word goes in the word for love

ma is a familiar word for mother

clue.text: Run The Times with an odd approach to attracting readers

clue.text: Slip perry and port out of their containers?

clue.text: Cat where birdies are to be had, we hear

explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat with tufted ears and a short tail.

clue.text: Desert allotment with no source of irrigation

clue.text: Aquatic bird, one occupying familiar position of dam
